content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the causal chain for the postmortem, starting with the symptom that account pages failed for many shoppers, then tracing how the error rate climbed from baseline through to its peak, citing the relevant metric for that spike.

I'm tracing the root cause down to the ZeroDivisionError thrown in the spend summary code starting around 14:59, then confirming it was the monthly-spend feature flag switch that routed traffic into that broken path—evidence from the flag evaluation logs and the fact that reverting it restored service. I'm also checking other candidate causes like deploys and rollout state, confirming no deploys occurred in the preceding day and that all replicas were running a single stable revision before onset, ruling those out as contributors.

Now I'm pinning down the mechanism: the monthly average calculation divides by this month's purchase count, so shoppers with prior purchases but none this month hit a zero-count division, raising the error at line 47—consistent with the stack trace location, though I still want to confirm the exact mechanism against other evidence rows.

I'm also noting the ramp-up pattern in the flag rollout (146 off/54 on at 14:59, then fully on by 15:00), which looks like a normal gradual deployment rather than something anomalous. As for contributing factors, there seems to be a gap in test coverage—no test exercised the monthly path for a shopper with zero purchases this month, since the existing test only expected the error for the lifetime path, and this gap is what let the bug slip through before the flag flipped on.

For CF-3, nobody was actually paged for the alert, but since Argus mitigated it quickly anyway, paging wouldn't have meaningfully shortened the incident — so it doesn't qualify as a real contributing factor, though it's worth noting as a gap in the went_wrong section rather than as an action item.

For action items, I'm drafting a proposal to stage flag rollouts like monthly-spend-feature in steps with automatic halting on error rate spikes, tied back to CF-2. I'm also trying to phrase the condition for re-enabling the flag — it needs the PR #336 fix deployed and its tests run first, though I'm debating whether to split that into separate items since review/merge is already a separate action.

For still_at_risk, I'm noting the division-by-zero bug is still live in the code, so re-enabling monthly-spend-feature would again break account pages for shoppers with no purchases that month.

For cause_in_plain_words, I'm framing it as: an admin switched on a new monthly spending summary feature that divides by the number of purchases this month, which breaks for shoppers who bought before but not this month.

For root_cause, I need to word it carefully to avoid spelling out "zero" as a number — I'll describe how the average_spend_per_item_this_month function divides spend by purchase count, which is unset for shoppers without purchases that month, causing the division error and failing the account page request.

I'm noting the timing gaps between the flag revert, the alert, and the Mitigation Agent's confirmation, plus the later draft PR from Code-Fix. For what went wrong, I'm flagging that nobody was paged and no on-call incident got linked to the alert.

For assumptions, I'm listing that the zero-count mechanism for shoppers came from Code-Fix's reading rather than an actual run, that the ZeroDivisionError at line 47 explains the error rise even though the logs are sampled rather than exhaustive, and that the pre-existing ClientDisconnected errors are unrelated baseline noise rather than part of the issue.

Now I'm building the citation chain: step 1 covers the rise in server error share for account page requests using AL1, Gbac1, and T5; step 2 covers the ZeroDivisionError appearing in spend_summary.py from onset using G5309 and Gad41.

Step 3 traces the monthly-spend-feature flag being switched on by admin at the onset time, sending traffic down the broken path, and switching it back off resolving the failures — ruling out deploys or other flag changes since the flag toggle was the only change that day. Step 4 will cover the mechanism itself, citing F1 and G5309.

Now I'm drafting the action items: staged rollout with automatic halting on account page error rate increases for prevention, plus requiring flag-enabled CI tests before production activation, and I'm starting on the detection recommendation.

Continuing to the detection item, I'm noting that routing the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call engineer doesn't have a direct answer, and similarly, keeping monthly-spend-feature off until the no-purchase fix ships doesn't map cleanly to an existing record, so I'm leaving that answer blank too. I'm also confirming that CF-1 is addressed by AI-2 since the PR adds tests, while CF-2 remains unaddressed.

action_items.item: Roll out io-shop feature flag changes, such as monthly-spend-feature, in stages that halt automatically when the account page error rate rises.
In CI, run the account page tests with each feature flag switched on, and require them to pass before that flag can be switched on in production.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop so that it pages the on-call person.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until a fix for shoppers with no purchases this month is deployed.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests failed. The share of requests answered with a server error went from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} while the service was broken, and peaked at {errors_at_worst}.
From the onset, account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. No such error was logged before the onset, when account pages rendered normally.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. No deploy came back for the day before the onset, and the flag switch was the only production change read.

The revision the replicas were running. All replicas ran one revision as of {T10.1}, and no deploy was read in the day before. The service was back to normal with that revision still in place once only the flag had been switched back off.
Another flag change. The flag provider's history shows one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour read: the switch of monthly-spend-feature.

causal_chain.step: From the onset, account page requests evaluated monthly-spend-feature as on, which sent them down the monthly spend summary code. Admin switched the flag on at {P1.1}. Evaluations were all off before then, partly on at {G971b.1}, and on from then until the alert. Switching the flag back off ended the failures.

With the flag on, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases made this month. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2}.

input.cause_in_plain_words: An administrator switched on a setting that adds a new monthly spending summary to shoppers' account pages, and that summary likely breaks because it divides by the number of purchases made this month, which is none for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.

contributing_factors.factor: No test was seen that runs the monthly spend summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month. In the files Code-Fix read, the existing test helper calls this shopper the ordinary case, and the only test seen that expects ZeroDivisionError covers the lifetime path for an account with no purchases ever.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have failed on the division before anyone switched the flag on in production, so the fault would have been caught before it reached shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for every evaluation within about a minute. No staged rollout and no check that stops a flag change when errors rise were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A staged rollout that halts when the account page error rate rises would have kept the failures to a small slice of shoppers and switched the flag back off sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Investigator tied the onset to the one production change it read: the switch of monthly-spend-feature.
The Mitigation Agent switched the flag back off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and confirmed the service was out of the incident's level {T21.1 - T18.1} after the revert.
Code-Fix proposed a fix as draft pull request PR #336 {T23.1 - T22.1} after the incident was marked mitigated.
went_wrong: The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, account pages call `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases flagged `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}, so the function raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.2} and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The faulty division is still in the running code, so switching monthly-spend-feature back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
